stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security threat identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attackers can distribute malicious payloads across multiple pull requests (PRs) to evade detection.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning.
It addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data like PII, necessitating reliable post-hoc removal.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not the internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It introduces 'LACUNA,' a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods beyond simple output-level checks.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, questioning whether existing parameter-targeting unlearning methods truly erase knowledge from the model's internal structure.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Addresses the high inference cost of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) used in state-of-the-art image/video generation.
Introduces OrbitQuant, a novel data-agnostic quantization method designed to overcome activation shifting issues in DiTs.
Bypasses the need for re-fitting calibration data across different checkpoints or modalities, simplifying deployment.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
Proposes 'LACUNA,' a new testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
Highlights a gap in current research: existing benchmarks only test output-level unlearning, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: NASA launched an emergency mission to stop the Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: NASA launched an emergency mission to save the Swift Observatory from atmospheric re-entry.
Recent solar storms have caused the observatory's orbit to drop, putting it at risk of burning up.
Katalyst Space Technologies was contracted to deploy a Link spacecraft for the interception mission.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-resistant tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to mitigate reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating online monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, showing competitive results in testing.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a training-free inference method designed to enhance long-context reasoning.
Focuses on bridging the gap between LLMs' ability to access long context and their ability to utilize that context meaningfully.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses.
Suggests that social context can induce latent objectives in agents even without explicit prompting.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the difficulty of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across 900+ characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of attributing spoken utterances to specific characters.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from a teacher model can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization in LLMs.
The proposed method aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating disagreement between the teacher and student models.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers capable of generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like SAT solvers (Glucose 4.1, CaDiCaL 3.0.0).
The SE-RRMs exhibit improved extrapolation capabilities when dealing with larger problem sizes in constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to detect latent objective emergence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of social context on LLM communication.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from privileged teachers in OPSD can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating policy disagreement rather than relying solely on dense supervision.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for creating controllable simulated agents.
The agents learn a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from discounted returns.
This controllability allows engineers to test autonomous systems by isolating variables and reproducing edge cases without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking expert annotations.
Proposes a Neuron-Aware Data Selection method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Uses the model's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks behave under non-IID conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of robustness in decentralized, large-scale machine learning systems.

stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks poorly suited for traditional coding.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to address drawbacks of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in complex video narratives.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to 'Typographic Attacks' (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a 'training-free' method for robust concept localization to address this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during multimodal reasoning.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to better attend to visual inputs when correcting previous errors.
Focuses on improving the ability of models to provide grounded corrections, especially for out-of-distribution visual data.

stories.title: TestEvo-Bench: An Executable and Live Benchmark for Test and Code Co-Evolution
stories.author: Pengyu Nie
bullet_points: Introduces TestEvo-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the co-evolution of software tests and code.
Addresses a gap in existing benchmarks by requiring tests to be executable and semantically tied to code changes, rather than relying on static metadata.
Aims to better assess whether test automation agents can correctly propagate changes from code modifications into the test suite.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates whether scaling up Large Language Models (LLMs) can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study questions if simulation accuracy is inherently tied to general LLM capabilities or if it requires separate research focus.
The authors utilize scaling laws to analyze the relationship between compute scale, general benchmarks, and simulation fidelity.

stories.title: My credential rule reported 842 secrets in vercel/ai. The real count was 0.
stories.author: ofri-peretz

The article discusses the technical challenge of moving from context-blind regex detection to context-aware security scanning, noting AI assistants can regenerate misleading strings.

stories.title: Agent Execution Protocol v1.1 — A microkernel runtime for LLM agents with watchdog timers and ACID transactions
stories.author: ferreiratechnology2025max
